newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Zaire's Kabila meets S.Africa's Mandela for talks.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Kabila meets S.Africa's Mandela for talks.

text.p: Zaire's rebel leader Laurent Kabila met South African President Nelson Mandela in Cape Town on Thursday in a last-ditch effort to avert a bloodbath in the country's seven-month old civil war.
Kabila landed in South Africa at sunset and was driven straight to Mandela's Tuynhuys office where officials said he was ushered directly into one-on-one talks with the president.

Mandela, bidding to rescue Zairean peace talks, sent a jet to the Angolan enclave of Cabinda to fetch the rebel leader, who on Wednesday refused at the last minute to meet Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko on a South African ship in the Congolese port of Pointe Noire, citing security concerns.

Presidential spokesman Parks Mankahlana said Mandela would stretch his patience to end the humanitarian tragedy unfolding in Zaire. "We think there is still a very large opening for them both to walk through to achieve peace in Zaire," he said.
Mandela has tabled a two-page proposal for a transition to democracy in Zaire after 32 years of Mobutu's autocratic rule, but Kabila has yet to respond.
In the Zaire capital of Kinshasa "bloodbath" was a word on many lips as the teeming capital of five million people prepared for the worst.
